findings.description: The inline policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", giving the user near-admin control over data in all S3 buckets (including Get/Put/Delete and bucket-policy changes) and other services. This violates least privilege and greatly expands the blast radius if the associated access key is compromised.

A long-term IAM access key is created for the user with no rotation or expiry, so the credential remains valid indefinitely. Combined with the wildcard policy, a single leaked key grants broad persistent access; short-term credentials via roles would be the secure alternative.

The IAM access key secret is surfaced through a Terraform output, which is written to console output and stored in plaintext-adjacent state/logs. Secrets should never be emitted as outputs; moreover, since no pgp_key is set, the plaintext secret attribute is persisted in the Terraform state.
